issues.description: The UML/specification requires Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal) to return a boolean, but the provided solution implements it with void return type. This creates ambiguity for students and makes it impossible to satisfy both the UML and a reference solution at the same time.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts to the same signature. Prefer updating the solution (and template stub if added) to `public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal)` and return `animals.add(animal)`, or update the UML/spec text to specify `void addAnimal(Animal animal)`.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method has its Animal parameter commented out, which prevents students from compiling if they follow the UML/spec that defines `singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal)`. The solution correctly includes the parameter, so the template and solution are structurally inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (and add the `Animal` type import or ensure it exists in the same package) so students can implement the verse logic without first repairing the method header.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies `Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal):boolean`, but the solution implements `addAnimal(Animal animal)` returning `void`. This mismatch makes it unclear to students whether they must return a success flag, and prevents direct mapping from the UML signature to the code they should write.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts to the same signature. Either (a) change UML/problem text to `addAnimal(animal: Animal):void`, or (b) change template/solution to `public boolean addAnimal(Animal animal) { return animals.add(animal); }`.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires implementing a getter and a setter for `Animal.name`, but does not specify the setter name; the solution uses `setName(String newName)` while the attribute is `name`. Students may expect `setName(String name)` (parameter name aligned) when following typical conventions and the UML's `name` identifier, creating minor mapping friction.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the setter parameter to match the conceptual identifier: `public void setName(String name) { this.name = name; }` (or specify `newName` explicitly in the problem statement to match the solution).
